lines.note: Môtô denotes a single hair of the head, then introduces a transferred sense of something minute. Both circumflexes are visible; this is the headword anticipated by the previous page's catchword.

runs.text: Couſa muito pouca como ponta de hum cabelo.

lines.note: The transferred sense is a very small amount, compared with the tip of a hair. This completes the Môtô entry.
Moto means a beginning or root. Qino mo- starts the example ki no moto, a tree's root, with its printed line-end division.
To completes moto and its tree-root gloss. A new sense follows, meaning formerly or from the beginning.
Des do principio completes the temporal sense. The historical separate des do is preserved rather than replaced by modern desde.

runs.text: Hũa doença das mãos com que in-

lines.note: Motobu names a hand ailment. The definition begins the description of swelling, physically dividing inchão across two rows; no modern diagnosis is inferred.
Chão os dedos completes the explanation that the fingers swell. It is the continuation of in- above, not a reference to the ground.
Motobune denotes the larger or principal vessel in a group. The comparison with the other boats continues below.

runs.text: em reſpeito de outras em que vão peßoas me-

lines.note: The principal vessel is distinguished from boats carrying people of lower standing. Me- is the printed beginning of menos, continued below.
Nos principaes completes menos principaes, less important people. This closes the comparison between the vessels and their occupants.
Motocubi is equated with Cubi and covers the neck or a severed head. The Portuguese relative clause continues below.
The head is described as cut off at the neck. The spelling pello is preserved with its doubled l.

runs.text: Cabedal com que hum começa de

lines.note: Motode denotes the capital with which someone starts trading. The scan has final l in Cabedal, not OCR i.
The capital enables trading or acquiring goods. The visible verb is granjear, correcting granjrar; the example starts Mo- at the line end.

The example means that trade cannot be carried on without capital. The intended lexical form is aqinaiua, but enlargement shows aq followed by a blank and the damaged naiua sequence; no i can be securely recovered between q and n. The aligned aq naiua is therefore retained as a nonblocking reading caveat rather than silently completed. The Portuguese begins Não a- and continues below.

runs.text: uendo cabedal não ſe pode fazer mercancia.

lines.note: The Portuguese confirms that without capital one cannot engage in trade. The first word completes a-uendo from the preceding row.

runs.text: Cabelos do toutiço que cuſtumão ter,

lines.note: Motodori refers to the hair or topknot retained at the back of the head. The gloss begins describing how Japanese people wear it.
The hair is kept and arranged as an ornament. The new example begins Moto- and continues with doriuo qiru on the next row.
Cutting the motodori is rendered as cutting the hair at the back. The scan reads detras, not OCR deuras.

runs.text: que he como raparſe, ou deixar o mundo.

lines.note: Cutting off that hair is compared with shaving the head or leaving worldly life. The gloss gives the social or religious significance of the action without changing the Japanese example.

runs.text: Ponta do arco da parte de baixo,

lines.note: Motofazu is the lower tip or nock of a bow. The visible word parte corrects OCR oarte.

runs.text: & a que lhe reſponde ẽ cima ſe diz,

lines.note: The corresponding upper end is called Vrafazu. The scan separates reſponde ẽ; the Japanese name occurs inside the Portuguese explanation and is not a new headword.
Motoi means a cause or motive. This semantic entry is separate from the homographic cross-reference immediately below.
A second Motoi is referred to Motoyui as the better form. Meliùs and Vide infrà are Latin editorial directions, retained with their printed accents.
Motome means seeking or inquiring. Its following paragraph adds the related sense of obtaining something.
The second sense is having or acquiring. The historical aquirir is retained without inserting the modern d.

Motomeye means obtaining or acquiring what one seeks. The scan has uru, not the malformed OCR uroj, and an undivided aquirir. Moto ſuye pairs beginning and end. The printed word space and long ſ are retained rather than treating it as an unbroken compound.

runs.text: Não ſe vſa mais que no nega-

lines.note: Motovori is said to occur only in a negative form. The usage restriction is divided after nega- and continues below.
Motovoranu fito is the negative example, describing a person who does not respond or take things in. Its Portuguese explanation starts Homem and continues for two rows.

runs.text: que eſtà como amuado, & não percebe, nem

lines.note: The person is as if sullen and does not understand or notice what is said. The printed amuado is meaningful here and is not an OCR repair target.

runs.text: faz caſo do que lhe dizem.

lines.note: The gloss concludes that the person pays no attention to what others say. This closes the explanation of the negative-only usage.

runs.text: Hum inſtrumento de corno, ou de

lines.note: Motovoxi is an implement made of horn or another material. The scan supports inſtrumento, correcting the malformed OCR infirumento.

runs.text: outra couſa que ſe tem na mão pera largar, ou

lines.note: The implement is held in the hand to let out or control a line. Its function, rather than just its material, is explained across the following rows.

runs.text: puxar por elle como por roldanazinha, o cordel,

lines.note: The cord is pulled through it as through a little pulley. The historical diminutive roldanazinha is retained as printed.

The cord is for falcons, establishing the falconry context of the implement. The terminal mark has a descending comma form in the scan; it is retained as a comma despite closing the definition before the next entry.
Motoyori means from the beginning and refers the reader back to Moto. Moto is a Japanese cross-reference embedded in the Portuguese-Latin explanatory sentence.

runs.text: Cabelos q̃ atão no toutiço os Iapoẽs.

lines.note: Motoyui is described here as hair tied at the back of the head by Japanese people. The visible capital I in Iapoẽs corrects OCR t; the definition itself is preserved rather than replaced by a modern dictionary gloss.
Motozzuqi means approaching or attaching oneself. The doubled zz and the printed principal forms are retained.
Ienno michini motozzuqu gives approaching the path of virtue. Ienno is understood through the virtuous-path gloss, not mechanically read with a vocalic initial I.

runs.text: ou entrar no caminho da virtude.

lines.note: The Portuguese completes the example as entering the path of virtue. This is the end of Motozzuqi, not an independent religious entry.

runs.text: Couſa inſofriuel, ou que não conuẽ.

lines.note: Mottainai is explained here as intolerable or improper. The damaged second t remains recoverable; the scan also supports continuous inſofriuel and the separate words que não conuẽ, correcting the garbled OCR.
Mottate is the verb for raising something. The printed tçuru principal form is kept rather than regularized to the preceding verb patterns.
A distinct noun Mottate names a defensive screen formerly used in war. The initial M is abraded but identifiable from its remaining strokes and the adjacent same-form entry; it is not Ai.

runs.text: te na guerra feito de taboas großas, ou bambus

lines.note: The screen was made of thick boards or bamboo. The first syllable completes antigamen-te from the preceding row.
The material was covered with cowhide. This completes the description of the old defensive screen.
Motte is labelled a preposition meaning with or by. The scan reads Prepoſição and per, not the OCR's Ereposição and pir; Ieſus- begins the example that continues at the top of column 2.
This completes Ieſus-no minauo motte from the preceding column: with the holy name of Jesus. The Portuguese name itself continues on the next physical row.

The omitted left-hand text de Ieſu. completes the Motte example. At the far right, (ordinaria. is a displaced continuation of extra- in Motteno foca on the following row. Both fragments are retained on their actual shared physical row, not reordered for syntax.
Motteno foca is glossed as something great or extraordinary. Extra- is completed by the displaced ordinaria. at the far right of the preceding physical row.
Mottomo is an adverb meaning with much reason or quite rightly. The double consonant is visible.
The repeated expression Mottomo mottomo has the same meaning. The scan supports m in the first occurrence where OCR produced Mottoio.
Môxen denotes felt or a carpet. The Portuguese reads Feltro and alcatifa, correcting the OCR's Feliro and alcariſa; the headword o has a circumflex.

runs.text: Voz com que ſe chama peßoa honrada

lines.note: Mǒxi is an expression used to attract the attention of an honoured person. Its first o has a caron, distinguishing it graphically from Môxi below.

runs.text: como quem diz, o lhe que lhe quero dizer.

lines.note: The gloss paraphrases the call as asking the addressee to listen to what the speaker wants to say. Diz corrects OCR oiz; the visible separation o lhe is retained despite the expected single word olhe.
Moxi is the unmarked adverb meaning perhaps or unless. The visible capital M corrects OCR N; no long-vowel mark is supplied from the neighbouring headwords.

runs.text: Hum dos cinco liuros que ha nomeados

lines.note: Môxi names the Chinese book associated with Mencius. The source calls it one of five named books; that numerical description is preserved, and the final word is read nomeados rather than OCR nomeadoà.
Na China completes the book's geographical description. The short row belongs to Môxi, not to the following verb.
Mǒxi gives the polite verb for speaking while honouring the addressee. Its caron and the printed ſu, ita principal forms are retained.
The scan reads quem ſe fala, correcting the OCR's misplaced letters and word divisions. Sonataſamaye mǒſu addresses an honoured you, matching the following Portuguese rendering.

runs.text: Falo com voßa merce. ¶ Item, Significa

lines.note: The translation is speaking to your honour. A new paragraph then introduces doing an action while humbling the speaker.

runs.text: fazer humilhandoſe o que fala. Vt,

lines.note: The definition explicitly says that the speaker humbles themself. The visible u corrects hamilhandoſe; the example begins Buſa- and continues below.
Buſata mǒxita means having committed a fault or omission, as the Portuguese confirms. The next example begins Reiuo mǒ- and continues with ſu on the following row.
Reiuo mǒſu is rendered as visiting or greeting someone. A further example begins Fito- at the right edge.
Fitoni mexi nandouo mǒſu means inviting someone to food or something similar. Co- is the physical start of the Portuguese comer.

runs.text: mer, ou outra couſa a alguem.

lines.note: This completes comer and the invitation gloss. The same polite-verb entry spans all these examples.

Moxiague means speaking to a noble person. The abraded o has no securely legible accent, so it remains unmarked. The clearly printed guru principal form is retained despite the different abbreviated form in the supplied lexical index.
Mǒxiai means speaking among themselves or together. The past-form o has a visible caron, correcting OCR yôta; the other o marks are likewise carons.
Mǒxi atçucai concerns handling or negotiating something verbally. The principal-form carons and the headword's word space are retained.
Ar de palaura completes negociar de palaura, negotiating by speech. The short row is part of the preceding definition.
Mǒxi auaxe means agreeing through discussion or consultation. The printed ſuru principal form and the physical division con- are retained.

runs.text: ſultando aßentar entre ſi algũa couſa.

lines.note: This completes consulting together and settling a matter by agreement. The printed aßentar and algũa remain unmodernized.
Mǒxicacari means beginning to speak. The final abbreviated atta form is visible and retained.
Mǒxicachi means prevailing in an argument or dispute. The scan separates Vencer na and contains no extra t, correcting Vencernta.
Contenda supplies the second Portuguese word for a dispute. This short continuation completes Mǒxicachi.
Mǒxicanaye means procuring fulfilment of someone's wish through speaking or intercession. The scan's yuru and historical Comprir are retained.

runs.text: &c. a alguem intercedendo por elle, ou con-

lines.note: The definition specifies interceding for someone. The abbreviation is &c., not &co; con- begins the following verb for granting something.
Granting something is the alternative means of fulfilling the request. Cono cotouo introduces the cited Japanese example.

runs.text: comacani catatte vaga vyeno ſoxôuo mǒ-

lines.note: The example asks for the matter to be explained in detail and for the speaker's petition to be satisfied. The circumflex in ſoxôuo is distinct from the caron in final mǒ-.
Xicanayete cudaſareyo completes the request for fulfilment. Qir. is the citation label; the Portuguese translation begins Praticã- and continues below.

runs.text: do eſtas couſas miudamente peço vos q̃ me fa-

lines.note: The translation asks for the matters to be discussed in detail. The physical divisions Praticã-do and fa-çais are preserved.
The petitioner asks that this petition be fulfilled. Historical comprir is retained consistently with the definition above.

Moxicaqe means attributing something to another person. The scan separates a uo-, producing the printed uo-tro across the break; this unusual order is not silently changed to outro. The abraded headword vowel is left unmarked where an accent is not established.
The example is making a slanderous accusation against someone. Fitoni and zanguenuo remain in the printed spelling, and mǒxicaqu- visibly carries a caron.
The Portuguese confirms bearing false witness against someone. Falſo has l followed by long ſ, not the OCR's double ſ.
Mǒxicaracuri means contriving verbal devices to persuade. Parafuſar is used figuratively in the gloss; the printed ru, utta forms remain unchanged.

runs.text: de inuençoens de palauras pera perſuadir al-

lines.note: The definition concerns inventions or contrivances of words used to persuade someone of something. Al- is continued by gũa on the following row.
Gũa completes algũa and the definition of persuading someone of a matter. It is a continuation, not a new headword.
Mǒxicaſume means obscuring something through words. The Portuguese noun couſa is divided after cou-.
The example concerns obscuring one's own fault. The scan shows final mǒ without an established terminal hyphen, so the OCR-supplied hyphen is removed.
This completes mǒxi caſumuru and renders it as excusing or covering up one's faults. The scan has a word space after xi, and the damaged Portuguese reads encobrir ſuas, not omobrir ſuar.
Faltas completes the object of covering up: one's faults or errors. The short continuation closes Mǒxicaſume.
Mǒxicatame means making a solid agreement or pact. The adjective firme is on the next row.
The pact is firm and made with another person. The scan supports firme and outro, correcting the OCR's frime and ouro; the catchword below is not part of this sentence.
